court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent were married in 2020 and have a child together. They are living separately due to misunderstandings. Respondent filed FCOP for restitution of conjugal rights before the Family Court, Vellore.

legal_principles.principle: The domicile or citizenship of the opposite party is immaterial in a case like this.
legal_principles.held: In case the marriage was solemnized under Hindu Law marital relationship is governed by the provisions of the Hindu Marriage Act. Therefore, Section 19 has to be given a purposeful interpretation.

legal_principles.principle: The residence of the wife determines the question of jurisdiction.
legal_principles.held: It is the residence of the wife, which determines the question of jurisdiction, in case the proceeding was initiated at the instance of the wife.

legal_principles.principle: The objects and reasons which prompted the parliament to incorporate a provision have to be taken note of.
legal_principles.held: While considering a provision like Section 19 (iii-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, the objects and reasons which prompted the parliament to incorporate such a provision has also to be taken note of.

legal_principles.principle: The difficulty faced by the wife in traveling or staying at a distant place is a relevant factor.
legal_principles.held: Experience is the best teacher. The Government found the difficulties faced by women in the matter of initiation of matrimonial proceedings.

outcome.final_order: Petition for transfer is allowed and FCOP No.85 of 2022 is transferred to the file of Sub Court, Arakkonam.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
Section 24 of the Civil Procedure Code
